card.summary_ko: 『삼국사기』 권44 「을지문덕」 열전 전문으로, 612년 수나라 침공 때 을지문덕이 적장 우중문에게 보냈다는 오언시와 살수대첩의 경과를 담고 있습니다.
card.summary_en: The full biography of Eulji Mundeok from Samguk sagi vol. 44, covering the 612 Sui invasion, the five-character poem he sent to the Sui general Yu Zhongwen, and the rout at the Salsu River.
card.edition_ko: 중국어 위키문헌 '三國史記/卷44' 중 「乙支文德」 (판 2150529, 2022-06-11). 원문은 퍼블릭 도메인, 전사는 CC BY-SA 4.0.

notes.ko:
**배경** 『삼국사기』는 김부식이 1145년경 인종의 명으로 편찬한 정사 형식의 역사서이며, 권44는 열전 제4로 을지문덕 등의 전기를 싣고 있습니다. 이 글은 고구려 영양왕 때인 612년 수 양제의 대군이 고구려를 침공한 전쟁(살수대첩)을 다룹니다. 수나라의 우문술과 우중문이 이끄는 별동대가 압록강을 건너 평양 가까이까지 진군했으나 을지문덕의 거짓 항복과 후퇴 전술에 지쳐 살수(청천강으로 보는 견해가 일반적)에서 크게 패했다고 합니다. 중국 쪽 사서에도 같은 전쟁이 기록되어 있습니다.

**의의** 제목의 「여수장우중문시」는 현존하는 우리 한시 가운데 가장 오래된 것의 하나로 꼽히는 시입니다. 이 시를 칭찬으로 적을 달래는 말로 읽는 해석도, 은근한 조롱으로 읽는 해석도 있습니다. 끝의 '論曰'은 김부식 자신의 평가입니다.

**형식과 주제** 인물 전기(열전)의 서사에 오언 4구의 시가 끼어 있고, 마지막에 사관의 논평이 붙는 구성입니다. 시의 '知足願云止'는 『노자』의 '知足不辱'을 떠올리게 하는 표현입니다.

**읽기 도움**
- 詐降: 거짓 항복.
- 虛實: 허와 실, 곧 내부 사정.
- 紿: 속이다.
- 北走: 패하여 달아나다 (北=배).
- 驟勝: 잇따른 승리.
- 方陣: 사각형 진.
- 鈔擊: 습격하다.
- 論曰: 사관의 평.
- 시 부분은 위키문헌에서 한 줄로 이어져 있습니다.
notes.en:
**Background** The Samguk sagi is the official-style history compiled by Kim Busik around 1145 on King Injong's order; vol. 44 is biographies (yeoljeon, no. 4) including Eulji Mundeok. This text covers the war of 612, when Emperor Yang of Sui invaded Goguryeo in the reign of King Yeongyang (the rout at the Salsu River). The Sui forces under Yuwen Shu and Yu Zhongwen crossed the Yalu and advanced near Pyongyang, but, worn down by Eulji Mundeok's feigned surrender and retreats, were crushed at the Salsu (usually identified with the Cheongcheon River). Chinese sources record the same war.

**Significance** The poem to the Sui general Yu Zhongwen (the title in the catalogue) is counted among the oldest surviving Korean poems in Literary Chinese. Some read it as courteous praise to talk the enemy out of fighting, others as veiled mockery. The closing 'Commentary' (論曰) is Kim Busik's own judgement.

**Form and themes** A biographical narrative into which a four-line, five-character poem is set, closed by the historian's comment. The phrase 'know contentment and wish to stop' recalls the Laozi's 'one who knows contentment is not disgraced'.

**Reading help**
- 詐降: feigned surrender.
- 虛實: strength and weakness, the real situation.
- 紿: to deceive.
- 北走: to flee in defeat (北 = to turn one's back).
- 驟勝: repeated victories.
- 方陣: square formation.
- 鈔擊: to raid, strike.
- 論曰: 'the commentary says'.
- In this Wikisource text the poem's four lines run together on one line.

paragraphs.orig: 乙支文德，未詳其世系。資沈鷙有智數，兼解屬文。隋開皇大業中，煬帝下詔征高句麗。於是，左翊衛大將軍宇文述，出扶餘道，右翊衛大將軍于仲文，出樂浪道，與九軍至鴨淥水。文德受王命，詣其營詐降，實欲觀其虛實。述與仲文，先奉密旨，若遇王及文德來，則執之，仲文等，將留之，尚書右丞劉士龍，為慰撫使，固止之，遂聽文德歸，深悔之，遣人紿文德曰：「更欲有議言，可復來。」文德不顧，遂濟鴨淥而歸。述與仲文，旣失文德，內不自安。述以粮盡欲還，仲文議以精銳追文德，可以有功，述止之。仲文怒曰：「將軍仗十萬兵，不能破小賊，何顔以見帝。」述等不得已而從之，度鴨淥水追之。文德見隋軍士有饑色，欲疲之，每戰輒北走，述等一日之中，七戰皆捷。旣恃驟勝，又逼群議，遂進東，濟薩水，去平壤城三十里，因山為營。文德遺仲文詩曰：

paragraphs.en: Eulji Mundeok: his lineage is unknown. By nature he was calm and bold, with wisdom and stratagems, and he also understood composing prose. In the Kaihuang and Daye eras of Sui, Emperor Yang issued an edict to attack Goguryeo. Thereupon Yuwen Shu, Grand General of the Left Yiwei, set out by the Buyeo road, and Yu Zhongwen, Grand General of the Right Yiwei, set out by the Nangnang road, and with nine armies they reached the Yalu River. Mundeok, on the king's command, went to their camp and feigned surrender, in truth wishing to observe their strengths and weaknesses. Shu and Zhongwen had earlier received secret instructions: if they met the king or Mundeok coming, they were to seize him. Zhongwen and the others were about to detain him, but Liu Shilong, Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, who was the pacification envoy, firmly prevented it, and so they allowed Mundeok to go back. They deeply regretted this and sent a man to deceive Mundeok: "We wish to discuss something further; you may come again." Mundeok did not look back; he crossed the Yalu and returned. Having lost Mundeok, Shu and Zhongwen were uneasy within. Because provisions were exhausted, Shu wished to withdraw; Zhongwen proposed pursuing Mundeok with elite troops, saying merit could be won, and Shu stopped him. Zhongwen said angrily, "General, relying on a hundred thousand troops, you cannot defeat a petty enemy; with what face will you see the emperor?" Shu and the others had no choice but to comply, and crossed the Yalu to pursue him. Mundeok saw hunger in the faces of the Sui soldiers and wished to wear them out; at every battle he turned and fled, and in a single day Shu and the others won seven battles. Relying on their repeated victories, and pressed by the opinions of the many, they advanced east, crossed the Sal River, and, thirty li from Pyongyang, camped against a mountain. Mundeok sent Zhongwen a poem, saying:

paragraphs.orig: 神策究天文妙算窮地理戰勝功旣高知足願云止
仲文答書諭之。文德又遣使詐降，請於述曰：「若旋師者，當奉王朝行在所。」述見士卒疲弊，不可復戰，又平壤城險固，難以猝拔，遂因其詐而還，為方陣而行。文德出軍，四面鈔擊之，述等且戰且行，秋七月至薩水，軍半濟，文德進軍，擊其後軍，殺右屯衛將軍辛世雄。於是，諸軍俱潰，不可禁止，九軍將士奔還，一日一夜，至鴨淥水，行四百五十里。初，度遼，凡軍三十萬五千人，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人。

paragraphs.en: Zhongwen replied with a letter admonishing him. Mundeok again sent an envoy to feign surrender, and requested of Shu: "If you withdraw your army, we shall escort our king to pay court at the emperor's place of sojourn." Shu saw that his officers and men were exhausted and could not fight again, and that Pyongyang was steep and strongly fortified and hard to take suddenly; so he took advantage of the feigned surrender and withdrew, marching in square formation. Mundeok sent out his troops and struck at them from all four sides; Shu and the others fought as they marched, and in autumn, the seventh month, reached the Sal River. When the army was half across, Mundeok advanced his troops and struck their rear army, killing Xin Shixiong, General of the Right Tunwei. Thereupon all the armies collapsed together and could not be stopped; the officers and men of the nine armies fled back, in one day and one night reaching the Yalu River, a march of four hundred and fifty li. At first, when they crossed the Liao, the armies numbered 305,000 in all; when they returned to Liaodong city, there were only 2,700.

paragraphs.orig: 論曰：煬帝遼東之役，出師之盛，前古未之有也，高句麗一偏方小國，而能拒之，不唯自保而已，滅其軍幾盡者，文德一人之力也。《傳》曰：「不有君子，其能國乎。」信哉。
paragraphs.reading: 논왈 양제요동지역 출사지성 전고미지유야 고구려일편방소국 이능거지 불유자보이이 멸기군기진자 문덕일인지력야 《전》왈 "불유군자 기능국호" 신재
paragraphs.en: Commentary: Emperor Yang's Liaodong campaign, the grandeur of the force he sent out, had no precedent in earlier ages. Goguryeo was a small state in one remote corner, yet it was able to resist him, and not merely to preserve itself: it destroyed that army almost to the last man, and this was the strength of Eulji Mundeok alone. The Commentary says, "Without gentlemen, could a state endure?" How true!
